column1: # Packages that install.sh bootstraps on Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie).
# Tab separated, one package per line, comments start with '#'. Plain data on
# purpose: install.sh reads this file, it is never sourced as shell code, so a
# package can be added or removed without touching install.sh or the tests.
#   tier     required = the applied dotfiles are broken or fall back to
#                       defaults without it, a failure fails the whole run
#            optional = everyday CLI/TUI, a failure is a warning
#   source   apt      = Debian 13 package, installed with apt-get
#            upstream = not in Debian 13, fetched from its official upstream
#            none     = not packaged for Debian 13 and not bootstrapped;
#                       used if it is already on PATH, otherwise skipped
#   package  name passed to apt-get (or the upstream project name)
#   command  executable Debian 13 actually provides, which is not always the
#            package name (fd-find ships fdfind, bat ships batcat, git-delta
#   why      which part of these dotfiles needs it
# Not bootstrapped on purpose: AI coding agents (Oh My Pi / omp, Claude Code,
# Codex CLI), language runtimes (Bun, Node.js, Python), Docker and other
# container runtimes, GUI applications, fonts, SSH keys and credentials.
